title: Check yourself: files in flight and a node you can't see into

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A DirPollAdaptor has poolSize 1 and pollInterval 2000. Its processor answers a file whose header is missing by throwing a DirPollException with setRetry(true). Over the next hour, good files keep arriving in request/. What happens to them?

options.text: They are processed as they arrive, since the retry wait runs on the polling thread and not in the pool
options.says: the wait of ten poll intervals runs on the pool thread that called the processor

options.text: They are held up to 20 seconds each, since the retry wait keeps the only pool thread busy
options.says: a retry waits pollInterval x 10 on the pool thread, and with one thread every file behind it waits; a missing header never improves

options.text: They are processed as they arrive, since DirPoll moves a file to bad/ after its third retry
options.says: DirPoll keeps no count of attempts; the file goes round until a person moves it

options.text: They are held until someone fixes the file, since DirPoll takes request/ in name order
options.says: the other files are processed between the retries, each delayed by up to ten poll intervals, not blocked for good

origin.section: 17.2 How the Processor Ends Decides Where the File Goes

questions.stem: Seven settlement files were in request/ when the node started; each takes the single pool thread 20 seconds. Thirty seconds later the supervisor sends SIGTERM and allows 90 seconds before a kill. What do you find in run/ after the JVM has exited?

options.text: Nothing, since Q2's shutdown hook lets the pool empty its queue before the JVM exits
options.says: the adaptor's stop ends the polling thread only; nothing waits for the pool or its queue

options.text: Nothing, since undeploying the adaptor moves unfinished files back to request/
options.says: nothing moves files out of run/, at stop or at start-up

options.text: Several files, since the pool keeps taking queued files until the JVM exits
options.says: the poller moved every file to run/ at once; the pool went on working during shutdown, so run/ holds files never started and possibly one already posted

options.text: Several files, since the pool stops at the signal and its current file is rolled back
options.says: the pool is not stopped; it starts new files during shutdown, and nothing rolls back work a processor has already committed

origin.section: 17.4 A Stop or a Crash Leaves Files in `run/`, Some of Them Already Done

questions.stem: A container's health probe runs the node's own jar with -c "ops:muxstat" every 30 seconds inside the container, and marks the node unhealthy when the output contains DOWN. The link to the acquirer drops at 14:00. What does the probe report?

options.text: DOWN within 30 seconds, since the command reads the node's MUXes through the NameRegistrar
options.says: the NameRegistrar belongs to one JVM; the probe's JVM has its own

options.text: DOWN within 30 seconds, since -c deploys the node's deploy/ files and their MUX cannot connect
options.says: with -c and no -d, Q2 deploys deploy-cli/, which has no MUX

options.text: Nothing wrong, since -c is refused while another Q2 runs in the same directory
options.says: -c runs its commands while the node runs in the same directory; it simply runs them in a JVM of its own

options.text: Nothing wrong, since the command runs in a new JVM whose registry holds no MUX
options.says: -c starts a second Q2 on deploy-cli/; the running node is read over its SSH CLI, JMX or a QBean inside it

origin.section: 17.5 A Command Sees Only the JVM It Runs In

questions.stem: SystemMonitor runs with sleepTime 600000 and wrote its last dump at 12:00:00. At 12:03 a garbage collection stops the JVM for 4 seconds. What drift does the 12:10 dump report?

options.text: About 4000 ms, since the monitor adds up the stops of the JVM between two dumps
options.says: drift is only how late the monitor's own wake-up was; it adds nothing up

options.text: About 4000 ms, since the pause stretched the monitor's sleep and it woke that much late
options.says: the sleep ends at its due time; a pause that ends minutes before the wake-up does not delay it

options.text: About 0 ms, since the pause ended long before the monitor was due to wake
options.says: drift shows a pause only where it covers the moment of waking; the GC log records every pause

options.text: About 0 ms, since drift counts a starved CPU and leaves garbage collection out
options.says: any pause that covers the wake-up shows, a collection included

origin.section: 17.6 `drift` Shows a Pause Only When It Covers the Monitor's Wake-Up

concepts: A -c command runs in a second JVM on deploy-cli/ and sees only its own registry; the running node is read over its SSH CLI.
SystemMonitor's drift shows a pause only where it covers the monitor's wake-up; the GC log records every pause.
A retry waits on a pool thread and DirPoll counts no attempts, so a file that can never improve stalls every file behind it and should be refused instead.
A stop or a crash leaves files in run/, some done and some never started, and nothing moves them back.
